clue.text: Small volume of overseas tourism

parts.note: read as a slim book that travellers abroad carry, holding handy sentences in a foreign language

explanation.surface: A slim report on the state of foreign travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocket guide of useful foreign expressions is the little book a traveller abroad takes along.

clue.text: Bus characters unruly after parking in these premises

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled letters behind the P

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

indicators.note: unruly letters are out of order, so the letters of bus are rearranged

parts.note: the characters (letters) of the word bus

explanation.surface: Passengers from a rowdy bus spill into the bars after it parks.
explanation.definitionFit: Licensed drinking houses are the premises the clue points at, a plural noun for bars.

clue.text: Free publication for delivery

definitions.meaning: to free a prisoner is to let them go
a new film, record or statement issued to the public

explanation.surface: A complimentary newspaper handed out to the doorstep.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to set loose and an issue put out to the public, such as a press statement or new album.

clue.text: Gradual deflation now Cup result is rectified

indicators.note: rectified means put right, so the letters of the fodder are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A team's spirits slowly sag as a cup result is corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is rectified' signals the anagram of NOW CUP RESULT; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre that loses air slowly through a small hole goes down gradually, a slow leak.

clue.text: Resting-place in France good and ready, perhaps

parts.note: bon is French for good

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word ready is in a possible other arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A French holiday spot that is pleasant and ready for guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A cemetery, colloquially, is where the dead are laid to rest.

clue.text: Loosened bosses' grip

indicators.note: loosened means freed up, so the letters of the employers' word are let fall into a new order

explanation.surface: The managers' hold on the company has slackened.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea that preoccupies the mind holds it fast, a verb of fixation.

clue.text: Tower maintenance

definitions.meaning: the strong central tower of a castle
the cost of food and upkeep, as in earning your board

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a castle's stronghold and also a person's upkeep, as in earning one's living expenses.

clue.text: Bigot's noble estate.

parts.note: Lord Bigot in Shakespeare's King John stands for the Bigod family, who held the title of Norfolk; the clue wants the rank of such a lord

explanation.surface: The country seat of an intolerant aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bigot' looks like a narrow-minded person; it is the historic Bigod name, Earls of Norfolk, spelt as in Shakespeare's King John.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank or lands of a peer below a marquess make up a count's territory, the dominion of that title.

clue.text: Pet to retrieve in Eastern growing-land?

parts.note: a pet is a fit of temper, as is a paddy in British slang
to field in cricket is to stop and return the ball

explanation.surface: Training a pet dog to fetch things in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like an animal; it means a sulk, a PADDY in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice is grown in flooded plots across Asia, so these wet fields are an oriental crop ground.

clue.text: One into hanging baskets?

parts.note: read not as a gardener but as someone keen on riding in the basket slung below an inflated envelope

explanation.surface: A gardening enthusiast keen on hanging baskets.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeronaut flying a hot-air craft travels in the basket suspended beneath the envelope.

clue.text: Poker drive

explanation.definitionFit: A jab or nudge pokes someone, and to urge an animal on is to drive it.

clue.text: Right place for a second grant

parts.note: right and real both work as intensifiers, as in a right mess or a real mess
a location is a place or site

explanation.surface: The proper spot for awarding a further subsidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Assigning funds again, a fresh distribution, is a renewed allotment or award.

clue.text: Force piano into inclined plane

parts.note: to ram something is to force it in
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Pushing a piano up onto a sloping board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is a link: the P follows RAM rather than going inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope joining two levels is a sloping surface, the simple machine of physics.

clue.text: Most recent history dead to Omar?

definitions.text: Most recent history dead to Omar?

parts.words: Most recent history dead to Omar?
parts.note: Omar Khayyam's Rubaiyat speaks of 'dead' past days set against unborn tomorrow, and the most recent past is the day before today

explanation.surface: Omar has no interest in recent history.
explanation.walkthrough: FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam has the line 'Unborn Tomorrow, and dead Yesterday'.
explanation.definitionFit: The day just gone is the latest slice of the past, which the poet calls dead.

clue.text: It shows how many men get in

definitions.text: It shows how many men get in

parts.words: It shows how many men get in
parts.note: read not as a door count but as a display of the runs scored, with men getting in as batsmen do

explanation.surface: A notice showing how many men are admitted to a venue.
explanation.definitionFit: At a cricket ground the display shows runs and wickets, the tally of batsmen who have gone in.

clue.text: Where you may be taken to if you have a marked suit

definitions.text: Where you may be taken to if you have a marked suit

parts.words: Where you may be taken to if you have a marked suit
parts.note: being taken to the ... means being fleeced, and a marked card suit suggests cheating at cards, while a stained garment goes for dry cleaning

explanation.surface: A card player with a marked suit gets taken somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken to the cleaners' is an idiom for being swindled; a stained suit also goes to a dry cleaner's.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry-cleaning shop is where a soiled garment is taken for washing.

clue.text: Old boys sporting a top-hat in reverse

parts.note: a lum hat is Scots for a top hat, lum being a chimney

indicators.note: in reverse means the little word in is written backwards

explanation.surface: Former pupils wearing a top hat back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reverse' turns IN into NI; LUM is the Scots word for a chimney, and a top hat is a lum hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Former pupils of a school or college are its graduates, its old boys.

clue.text: Take cover from file and look up "Nonsense"

parts.note: a folder is the card cover that holds a file

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for look is read from bottom to top

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Shield yourself with a file and look up the word nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Trifling foolishness or frippery is rubbish, empty talk.

clue.text: Arrhythmic playing gives polish at end of concerto

parts.note: to rub something is to polish it

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word concerto

explanation.surface: A performance that falters in rhythm makes up for it by shining in the finale.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who stretches and shortens beats expressively departs from strict tempo, playing freely in time.

clue.text: Shantyman Tom coming in from one end

definitions.meaning: The sailor of Dibdin's sea song
in cricket the bowler runs in from one end of the pitch

explanation.surface: A sea-shanty singer called Tom arrives from one end.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Bowling is Charles Dibdin's sea song; in cricket, bowlers deliver from one end at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: The sailor of the old sea song shares his surname with the cricket action of delivering the ball from one end.

clue.text: Slack, sometimes, about deficit! which is enormous

indicators.note: about means going round, so the coal word wraps the deficit word

parts.note: slack is coal dust, small pieces of coal
a deficit is a loss

explanation.surface: Lazy talk about a debt that turns out to be huge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sometimes' warns that slack is only one kind of COAL; SLACK is coal dust.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vast or gigantic in scale is immense, like the Colossus of Rhodes.

clue.text: Litter in clubs perhaps? Help to get the paper out

definitions.text: Help to get the paper out

indicators.note: in places the bedding inside the card suit

parts.note: clubs are one suit in a pack of cards
litter is straw bedding for animals

explanation.surface: Rubbish in the nightclubs? Someone must help get the newspaper out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like rubbish; it is straw BED for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Preparing copy for publication by checking and correcting it is the work of a newspaper editor's assistant.

clue.text: Abuse of one in business

indicators.note: in places the letter for one inside the business word

parts.note: trade is business or commerce
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Mistreatment of an employee at a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech of insults is a harangue, verbal invective.

clue.text: Australian flier in shady place with girl friend

parts.note: a bower is a shady leafy shelter in a garden
bird is British slang for a girlfriend or young woman

explanation.surface: An Australian pilot relaxing in an arbour with his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRD is British slang for a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: This species from Australia and New Guinea builds a decorated nest to court mates, so it flies there.

clue.text: Old pulpit plucked from Durham bonfire

indicators.note: plucked from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ancient lectern pulled out of a fire in the North of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Durham is a cathedral city in north-east England, apt for church furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: In early Christian churches a raised reading desk or stand was used for the lessons, a forerunner of the lectern.

clue.text: God of noise abatement?

parts.note: noise abated completely comes to nothing, zero, the letter O
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Which deity looks after quietening the racket?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as O DIN, no noise; the chief Norse god.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief of the Norse pantheon, father of Thor, is a deity.

clue.text: Dry fresh air before break of day

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters of air are made anew in another order
break of day is the start of the word day, its first letter

explanation.surface: Crisp fresh air before dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert land with no rainfall is parched, lacking moisture.

clue.text: Just like Barnum?

definitions.meaning: the showman P. T. Barnum ran circuses and shows, so he looked after a fair

explanation.surface: Simply like the famous American showman.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnum was a 19th-century American circus showman, so cryptically he 'minded a fair'.
explanation.definitionFit: An impartial person is even-handed and unbiased, and a showman who tended a funfair 'minded' one.

clue.text: Villains' shadows

definitions.meaning: a dirty dog is a rogue or scoundrel
to shadow someone is to follow them closely

explanation.definitionFit: Scoundrels are called curs, and to tail a suspect is to follow them like a hound.

clue.text: Being told about northern terrier

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Being informed about a dog from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' scrambles BEING TOLD into BEDLINGTO; the breed is named after a Northumberland town.
explanation.definitionFit: This lamb-like dog from north-east England is a breed of the earth-dog group.
